answer: Before an agent can trade, it must lock a bond that peers slash the instant its key signs two conflicting ledgers. Sybils therefore cost capital: a thousand fake workers need a thousand separate bonds, not one. Each bond is anchored to a unique capability token, so copying a willow seedling into a hundred wallets still spends a hundred deposits. A canyon of relay nodes and a tundra of dormant identities cannot be conjured for free; the attacker funds every shadow up front and forfeits the whole pile at the first double-sign.
